name: Example: Finding the First Few Terms of an Expansion With Negative Coefficients
problem: Find the first three terms of the binomial expansion of ${( x - 3y )}^ 5.$
worked_solution:
The binomial theorem states that for any positive integer $n,$ we have

 

$$
{(a + b)^n} = {n \choose 0}{a^n}{b^0} + {n \choose 1}{a^{n - 1}}{b^1} + {n \choose 2}{a^{n - 2}}{b^2} +  \cdots  + {n \choose n}{a^0}{b^n}.
$$

In the case of ${(x - 3y)}^ 5,$ we have  $a=x,$ $b=-3y ,$ and $n=5.$ 

Therefore, the first three terms of ${(x - 3y)}^ 5$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3y)^{5} & =(\frac{5}{0})(x)^{5}(-3y)^{0}+(\frac{5}{1})(x)^{5-1}(-3y)^{1}+(\frac{5}{2})(x)^{5-2}(-3y)^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1(x)^{5}+5(x)^{4}(-3y)+10(x)^{3}(9{y}^{2})+⋯ \\  & ={x}^{5}-15{x}^{4}y+90{x}^{3}{y}^{2}+⋯\end{aligned}
$$
